```text
Add a waitlist for fully-booked time slots
zach-short
zachbowden
enhancement,effort:high,scope: xl,type: feature
OPEN
-----
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When every slot on a booking page is taken, the page is a dead end. It renders `"no_available_slots": "No available slots"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2239`) or `"all_booked_today": "All booked."` (`:735`), and the visitor leaves with nothing to do.

Two things are lost at that moment. The visitor has no way to signal that they wanted this host and this week, so they go and book elsewhere. And the host never learns that the demand existed — a fully-booked page and a page nobody visited look identical from the dashboard.

Meanwhile the product already handles the other half well: bookings get cancelled and rescheduled all the time, and those freed slots currently go to whoever happens to reload the page first.

There is no waitlist anywhere in the codebase — `rg -ni "waitlist|waiting.list"` across the repo, excluding `node_modules` and lock files, returns zero matches.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let a visitor join a waitlist instead of hitting the dead end:

- on a fully-booked booking page, offer "join the waitlist" for a specific slot or for a date;
- when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled away, notify waitlisted people in order with a **time-limited claim link**, so a slot is not held forever by someone who has stopped watching;
- give hosts a per-event-type toggle, a cap on waitlist size, and a view of who is waiting;
- let people leave the waitlist from the notification.

This benefits both sides: attendees stop refreshing, and hosts convert cancellations into bookings instead of into gaps.

### User story

As someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for the time I need, so that I am told when it frees up instead of having to keep checking the page.

### Rough scope

**XL.** It needs a new Prisma model and migration, a hook into the cancel and reschedule paths to detect a released slot, notification delivery, an expiring claim flow that has to resolve a race between claimants, host settings UI, attendee UI, and i18n — and it must respect `EventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222`) rather than assuming one booking per slot.

### Source

Reviewing the booking page's own empty-state strings while verifying the local setup on 2026-09-14: the product ships copy for "all booked" and has nothing behind it.

### Additional context

Intended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: xl`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:high`. I do not have permission to apply labels to this repo, so they are recorded here until someone with triage access can add them.
```

```text
---
name: cal-diy-vitest-test-setup
description: "Vitest 4.1 ignores vitest.workspace.ts here, so only packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts runs; apps/web component tests must mock next/navigation and useLocale themselves."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fdfddafb-9974-4ccb-be41-6cd000a62bd6
  modified: 2026-10-29T23:48:12.128Z
---

This repo runs Vitest 4.1, which ignores `vitest.workspace.ts`. Every test runs under the root `vitest.config.mts`, whose only setup file is `packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts`. That file provides the jest-dom matchers and a ResizeObserver polyfill. The per-project setups named in the workspace file, such as `packages/ui/components/test-setup.tsx` with its next/navigation, useLocale and useIsPlatform mocks, never run.

**Why:** anything that renders `@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog` throws "invariant expected app router to be mounted" unless the test file mocks `next/navigation`'s `useRouter` itself. `EditLocationDialog.test.tsx` and `RescheduleDialog.test.tsx` both do this.

**How to apply:**
- When writing an `apps/web` component test, mock `next/navigation` (`useRouter`) and `@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale` in the test file.
- Run a single file with `yarn test <path>`. The script sets TZ=UTC, so the command also works in PowerShell.
- To type-check one test file with a temporary tsconfig placed outside the repo, set `typeRoots` to the repo's `node_modules/@types`. Otherwise `@types/jest` and `@types/testing-library__jest-dom` go missing and you get false errors.

Type checking on Julissa's Windows machine:
- `yarn type-check:ci --force` fails there with `spawn tsc ENOENT`. The `tsc-absolute` wrapper can't launch tsc on Windows, so this is a tooling problem, not a code problem.
- That run also re-formats `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` to LF line endings, a change with no content difference. Undo it with `git restore`.
- Instead, type-check the web app with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false -p apps/web/tsconfig.json` (~72s, the same heap CI uses).

Running a teammate's PR tests without touching Julissa's checkout (worked 2026-10-29 for PR #120):
- In the scratchpad, `git clone --shared --no-checkout` her repo. Fetch `pull/<n>/head` from GitHub into the clone and check it out with `core.longpaths=true`.
- Make `<clone>/node_modules` a real directory of junctions to her installed entries. Point the `@calcom/*` packages the PR changes at the clone. Point every other `@calcom/*` at her install, because a bare checkout lacks generated files such as `@calcom/prisma/enums`.
- From the clone, run `TZ=UTC node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run <files>` without going through yarn.
- Afterwards, remove the junctions with non-recursive `rmdir`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Remove-Item -Recurse` can follow junctions and delete their targets.
- `vitest.config.mts` has no `@components/*` alias, so the real `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal` can't load in tests. A review-only config that adds the alias works. The render also needs Radix `TooltipProvider`, because PasswordField uses a tooltip.

Local database facts, verified 2026-10-29:
- Julissa's dev DB runs in docker container `prisma-postgres-1` (postgres:18) and is reached at `localhost:5450/calendso` via `.env`. `packages/prisma/.env` is a symlink to the root `.env`.
- Running the Prisma CLI from the repo root fails with "conflict between env vars in .env and packages\prisma\.env", so run it from `packages/prisma`.
- An inline `DATABASE_URL`/`DATABASE_DIRECT_URL` overrides `.env`. `migrate status` prints a `Datasource … at host:port` line, which is the safe pre-flight check.
- `@calcom/prisma`'s `build` script (`auto-migrations.ts`) runs `migrate deploy` against the `.env` DB unless `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1`. So `yarn build` migrates the dev DB. `type-check:ci` only runs post-install, so it doesn't.
- Avoid `db-migrate` (migrate dev), `db-reset`, `db-nuke` and `dx` against the dev DB.
```

```text
305	+        ...data,
306	+        id: ++seq,
307	+        uid: `uid-${seq}`,
308	+        status: WaitlistStatus.WAITING,
309	+        hostUserId: null,
310	+        offerStart: null,
311	+        offerEnd: null,
312	+        offerExpiresAt: null,
313	+        createdAt: seq,
314	+      };
315	+      rows.push(row);
316	+      return row;
317	+    },
318	+    findByUid: async (uid: string) => rows.find((r) => r.uid === uid) ?? null,
319	+    findById: async (id: number) => rows.find((r) => r.id === id) ?? null,
320	+    findOldestWaitingForTime: async (q: { eventTypeId: number; time: Date }) =>
321	+      rows
322	+        .filter(
323	+          (r) =>
324	+            r.status === WaitlistStatus.WAITING &&
325	+            r.eventTypeId === q.eventTypeId &&
326	+            (r.slotStart
327	+              ? r.slotStart.getTime() === q.time.getTime()
328	+              : r.dayStart <= q.time && r.dayEnd > q.time)
329	+        )
330	+        .sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt)[0] ?? null,
331	+    transition: async (id: number, from: WaitlistStatus, to: WaitlistStatus, offer?: Offer | null) => {
332	+      const row = rows.find((r) => r.id === id);
333	+      if (!row || row.status !== from) return false;
334	+      row.status = to;
335	+      if (offer === null)
336	+        Object.assign(row, { hostUserId: null, offerStart: null, offerEnd: null, offerExpiresAt: null });
337	+      else if (offer) Object.assign(row, offer);
338	+      return true;
339	+    },
340	+    findEventTypeForWaitlist: async (id: number) =>
341	+      id === 1
342	+        ? {
343	+            id: 1,
344	+            title: "Intro call",
345	+            slug: "intro",
346	+            length: 30,
347	+            team: null,
348	+            owner: { username: "host" },
349	+            users: [],
350	+          }
351	+        : null,
352	+    createSlotHold: async (h: { uid: string; releaseAt: Date }) => {
353	+      holds.push({ uid: h.uid, releaseAt: h.releaseAt });
354	+    },
355	+    deleteSlotHolds: async (uid: string) => {
356	+      for (let i = holds.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (holds[i].uid === uid) holds.splice(i, 1);
357	+    },
358	+    findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt: async () => bookedEmails,
359	+    findActiveBookingStartTimes: async (q: { from: Date; to: Date }) =>
360	+      bookedTimes.filter((t) => t >= q.from && t < q.to),
361	+  };
362	+  return {
363	+    repo: repo as unknown as WaitlistRepository,
364	+    rows,
365	+    holds,
366	+    bookedTimes,
367	+    setBooked: (emails: string[] | null) => {
368	+      bookedEmails = emails;
369	+    },
370	+  };
371	+}
372	+type Offer = { hostUserId: number; offerStart: Date; offerEnd: Date; offerExpiresAt: Date };
373	+

543	diff --git a/packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.ts b/packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.ts
544	new file mode 100644
545	index 0000000000..adebc4213c
546	--- /dev/null
547	+++ b/packages/features/waitlist/services/WaitlistService.ts
548	@@ -0,0 +1,226 @@
549	+import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
550	+import { ErrorWithCode } from "@calcom/lib/errors";
551	+import { WaitlistStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
552	+import type { WaitlistEntryDto, WaitlistRepository } from "../repositories/WaitlistRepository";
553	+
554	+type FreedSlot = { eventTypeId: number; hostUserId: number; start: Date; end: Date };
555	+
556	+export const WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS = 6 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
557	+
558	+export type WaitlistOfferEmailData = {
559	+  name: string;
560	+  email: string;
561	+  timeZone: string;
562	+  eventTitle: string;
563	+  offerStart: Date;
564	+  offerExpiresAt: Date;
565	+  claimUrl: string;
566	+  leaveUrl: string;
567	+};
568	+
569	+export interface IWaitlistServiceDeps {
570	+  waitlistRepo: WaitlistRepository;
571	+  webappUrl: string;
572	+  scheduleOfferExpiry: (entryId: number, at: Date) => Promise<unknown>;
573	+  sendOfferEmail: (data: WaitlistOfferEmailData) => Promise<unknown>;
574	+  now?: () => number;
575	+}
576	+
577	+export class WaitlistService {
578	+  constructor(private deps: IWaitlistServiceDeps) {}
579	+
580	+  private now() {
581	+    return this.deps.now ? this.deps.now() : Date.now();
582	+  }
583	+
584	+  /** `date` is YYYY-MM-DD in the booker's `timeZone`; `slotStart` narrows the entry to one specific time. */
585	+  async join(input: {
586	+    eventTypeId: number;
587	+    name: string;
588	+    email: string;
589	+    timeZone: string;
590	+    date: string;
591	+    slotStart?: Date;
592	+  }) {
593	+    const dayStart = dayjs.tz(input.date, input.timeZone).startOf("day");
594	+    const dayEnd = dayStart.add(1, "day");
595	+    const slotStart = input.slotStart ?? null;
596	+    if (slotStart && (slotStart < dayStart.toDate() || slotStart >= dayEnd.toDate())) {
597	+      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Waitlist time must fall on the selected day");
598	+    }
599	+    const latestStart = slotStart ? slotStart.getTime() : dayEnd.valueOf();
600	+    if (latestStart - this.now() <= WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS) {
601	+      throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.BadRequest("Waitlist is not available less than 6 hours in advance");
602	+    }
603	+
604	+    const eventType = await this.deps.waitlistRepo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(input.eventTypeId);
605	+    if (!eventType) throw ErrorWithCode.Factory.NotFound(`Event type ${input.eventTypeId} not found`);
606	+
607	+    const email = input.email.toLowerCase();
608	+    const existing = await this.deps.waitlistRepo.findWaitingByEmailAndDay({
609	+      eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId,
610	+      email,
611	+      dayStart: dayStart.toDate(),
612	+      slotStart,
613	+    });
614	+    if (existing) return existing;
615	+
616	+    return this.deps.waitlistRepo.create({
617	+      eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId,
618	+      name: input.name,
619	+      email,
620	+      timeZone: input.timeZone,
621	+      dayStart: dayStart.toDate(),
622	+      dayEnd: dayEnd.toDate(),
623	+      slotStart,
624	+    });
625	+  }
626	+
627	+  /** Start times of this event type's bookings that could still be waitlisted (more than 6 hours away). */
628	+  async getBookedTimes(input: { eventTypeId: number; from: Date; to: Date }): Promise<Date[]> {
629	+    const earliest = new Date(this.now() + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
630	+    const from = input.from > earliest ? input.from : earliest;
631	+    if (from >= input.to) return [];
632	+    return this.deps.waitlistRepo.findActiveBookingStartTimes({
633	+      eventTypeId: input.eventTypeId,
634	+      from,
635	+      to: input.to,
636	+    });
637	+  }
638	+
639	+  /** Offers a freed slot to the longest-waiting person for that day and holds it for them. */
640	+  async offerSpot(slot: FreedSlot): Promise<number | null> {
641	+    const now = this.now();
642	+    // A slot starting within the claim window can't be held for the full 6 hours, so it isn't offered
643	+    if (slot.start.getTime() - now < WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS) return null;
644	+
645	+    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
646	+    if (
647	+      await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({ eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId, startTime: slot.start })
648	+    ) {
649	+      return null;
650	+    }
651	+
652	+    const entry = await repo.findOldestWaitingForTime({ eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId, time: slot.start });
653	+    if (!entry) return null;
654	+
655	+    const offerExpiresAt = new Date(now + WAITLIST_CLAIM_WINDOW_MS);
656	+    const won = await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, {
657	+      hostUserId: slot.hostUserId,
658	+      offerStart: slot.start,
659	+      offerEnd: slot.end,
660	+      offerExpiresAt,
661	+    });
662	+    // Another offer grabbed this entry concurrently; give the slot to the next person instead
663	+    if (!won) return this.offerSpot(slot);
664	+
665	+    await repo.createSlotHold({
666	+      uid: entry.uid,
667	+      eventTypeId: slot.eventTypeId,
668	+      userId: slot.hostUserId,
669	+      start: slot.start,
670	+      end: slot.end,
671	+      releaseAt: offerExpiresAt,
672	+    });
673	+    await this.deps.scheduleOfferExpiry(entry.id, offerExpiresAt);
674	+
675	+    const eventType = await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(slot.eventTypeId);
676	+    await this.deps.sendOfferEmail({
677	+      name: entry.name,
678	+      email: entry.email,
679	+      timeZone: entry.timeZone,
680	+      eventTitle: eventType?.title ?? "",
681	+      offerStart: slot.start,
682	+      offerExpiresAt,
683	+      claimUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/claim?uid=${entry.uid}`,
684	+      leaveUrl: `${this.deps.webappUrl}/api/waitlist/leave?uid=${entry.uid}`,
685	+    });
686	+    return entry.id;
687	+  }
688	+
689	+  async expireOffer(entryId: number) {
690	+    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
691	+    const entry = await repo.findById(entryId);
692	+    if (!entry || entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED || !entry.offerStart) return;
693	+
694	+    await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
695	+    const bookedEmails = await repo.findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt({
696	+      eventTypeId: entry.eventTypeId,
697	+      startTime: entry.offerStart,
698	+    });
699	+    if (bookedEmails) {
700	+      // Someone else booked during the hold: the waitlister keeps their place for the day
701	+      const claimed = bookedEmails.includes(entry.email.toLowerCase());
702	+      await repo.transition(
703	+        entry.id,
704	+        WaitlistStatus.OFFERED,
705	+        claimed ? WaitlistStatus.CLAIMED : WaitlistStatus.WAITING,
706	+        claimed ? undefined : null
707	+      );
708	+      return;
709	+    }
710	+
711	+    if (await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.EXPIRED)) {
712	+      await this.offerToNext(entry);
713	+    }
714	+  }
715	+
716	+  /** Returns false if the entry is unknown or already finished. */
717	+  async leave(uid: string): Promise<boolean> {
718	+    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
719	+    const entry = await repo.findByUid(uid);
720	+    if (!entry) return false;
721	+
722	+    if (entry.status === WaitlistStatus.WAITING) {
723	+      return repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.WAITING, WaitlistStatus.LEFT);
724	+    }
725	+    if (entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED) return false;
726	+    if (!(await repo.transition(entry.id, WaitlistStatus.OFFERED, WaitlistStatus.LEFT))) return false;
727	+
728	+    await repo.deleteSlotHolds(entry.uid);
729	+    await this.offerToNext(entry);
730	+    return true;
731	+  }
732	+
733	+  /** Booking page URL with the held slot preselected, or null when there is no live offer. */
734	+  async getClaimUrl(uid: string): Promise<string | null> {
735	+    const repo = this.deps.waitlistRepo;
736	+    const entry = await repo.findByUid(uid);
737	+    if (
738	+      !entry ||
739	+      entry.status !== WaitlistStatus.OFFERED ||
740	+      !entry.offerStart ||
741	+      !entry.offerExpiresAt ||
742	+      entry.offerExpiresAt.getTime() <= this.now()
743	+    ) {
744	+      return null;
745	+    }
746	+
747	+    const eventType = await repo.findEventTypeForWaitlist(entry.eventTypeId);
748	+    if (!eventType) return null;
749	+    const owner = eventType.team?.slug
750	+      ? `team/${eventType.team.slug}`
751	+      : (eventType.owner?.username ?? eventType.users[0]?.username);
752	+    if (!owner) return null;
753	+
754	+    const localStart = dayjs(entry.offerStart).tz(entry.timeZone);
755	+    const params = new URLSearchParams({
756	+      month: localStart.format("YYYY-MM"),
757	+      date: localStart.format("YYYY-MM-DD"),
758	+      slot: entry.offerStart.toISOString(),
759	+      name: entry.name,
760	+      email: entry.email,
761	+    });
762	+    return `${this.deps.webappUrl}/${owner}/${eventType.slug}?${params.toString()}`;
763	+  }
764	+
765	+  private async offerToNext(entry: WaitlistEntryDto) {
766	+    if (!entry.hostUserId || !entry.offerStart || !entry.offerEnd) return;
767	+    await this.offerSpot({
768	+      eventTypeId: entry.eventTypeId,
769	+      hostUserId: entry.hostUserId,
770	+      start: entry.offerStart,
771	+      end: entry.offerEnd,
772	+    });
773	+  }
774	+}
775	diff --git a/packages/features/waitlist/services/getWaitlistService.ts b/packages/features/waitlist/services/getWaitlistService.ts
776	new file mode 100644
777	index 0000000000..4ad8069e27
778	--- /dev/null
779	+++ b/packages/features/waitlist/services/getWaitlistService.ts
780	@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
781	+import WaitlistSpotOpenedEmail from "@calcom/emails/templates/waitlist-spot-opened-email";
782	+import tasker from "@calcom/features/tasker";
783	+import { getTranslation } from "@calcom/i18n/server";
784	+import { WEBAPP_URL } from "@calcom/lib/constants";
785	+import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";
786	+import { WaitlistRepository } from "../repositories/WaitlistRepository";
787	+import { WaitlistService } from "./WaitlistService";
788	+
789	+export function getWaitlistService() {
790	+  return new WaitlistService({
791	+    waitlistRepo: new WaitlistRepository(prisma),
792	+    webappUrl: WEBAPP_URL,
793	+    scheduleOfferExpiry: (entryId, at) =>
794	+      tasker.create("expireWaitlistOffer", { entryId }, { scheduledAt: at }),
795	+    sendOfferEmail: async (data) => {
796	+      // shortcut: entries don't store a locale, so offers are always English; store one at join time to localize
797	+      const t = await getTranslation("en", "common");
798	+      return new WaitlistSpotOpenedEmail({ ...data, t }).sendEmail();
799	+    },
800	+  });
801	+}
802	diff --git a/packages/prisma/migrations/20261029120000_add_waitlist_entry/migration.sql b/packages/prisma/migrations/20261029120000_add_waitlist_entry/migration.sql
803	new file mode 100644
804	index 0000000000..036a17c47d
805	--- /dev/null
806	+++ b/packages/prisma/migrations/20261029120000_add_waitlist_entry/migration.sql
807	@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
808	+-- CreateEnum
809	+CREATE TYPE "WaitlistStatus" AS ENUM ('WAITING', 'OFFERED', 'CLAIMED', 'EXPIRED', 'LEFT');
810	+
811	+-- CreateTable
812	+CREATE TABLE "WaitlistEntry" (
813	+    "id" SERIAL NOT NULL,
814	+    "uid" TEXT NOT NULL,
815	+    "eventTypeId" INTEGER NOT NULL,
816	+    "name" TEXT NOT NULL,
817	+    "email" TEXT NOT NULL,
```

```text
58	+  response.cookies.set("uid", uid, {
59	+    path: "/",
60	+    sameSite: useSecureCookies ? "none" : "lax",
61	+    secure: useSecureCookies,
62	+  });
63	+  return response;
64	+}

109	+import { getWaitlistService } from "@calcom/features/waitlist/services/getWaitlistService";
110	+import { checkRateLimitAndThrowError } from "@calcom/lib/checkRateLimitAndThrowError";
111	+import getIP from "@calcom/lib/getIP";
112	+import { piiHasher } from "@calcom/lib/server/PiiHasher";
113	+import { defaultResponderForAppDir } from "app/api/defaultResponderForAppDir";
114	+import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";

116	+import { z } from "zod";
117	+
118	+const joinWaitlistSchema = z.object({
119	+  eventTypeId: z.number().int(),
120	+  name: z.string().trim().min(1).max(255),
121	+  email: z.string().email(),
122	+  timeZone: z.string().refine((tz) => Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone").includes(tz) || tz === "UTC"),
123	+  date: z.string().regex(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/),
124	+  slotStart: z.coerce.date().optional(),
125	+});
126	+
127	+async function handler(req: NextRequest) {
128	+  const parsed = joinWaitlistSchema.safeParse(await req.json().catch(() => null));
129	+  if (!parsed.success) {
130	+    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, message: "Invalid request" }, { status: 400 });
131	+  }
132	+
133	+  await checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
134	+    rateLimitingType: "core",
135	+    identifier: `api:waitlist-join:${piiHasher.hash(getIP(req))}`,
136	+  });
137	+
138	+  await getWaitlistService().join(parsed.data);
139	+  return NextResponse.json({ success: true }, { status: 200 });
140	+}

460	diff --git a/apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useWaitlistBookedTimes.ts b/apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useWaitlistBookedTimes.ts
461	new file mode 100644
462	index 0000000000..67c31a4379
463	--- /dev/null
464	+++ b/apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useWaitlistBookedTimes.ts
465	@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
466	+import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
467	+import { useBookerStoreContext } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/BookerStoreProvider";
468	+import { useBookerTime } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/hooks/useBookerTime";
469	+import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
470	+import { useMemo } from "react";
471	+
472	+/** Booked (waitlistable) start times of the current event, grouped by YYYY-MM-DD in the booker's timezone. */
473	+export const useWaitlistBookedTimes = (): Record<string, string[]> => {
474	+  const eventId = useBookerStoreContext((state) => state.eventId);
475	+  const month = useBookerStoreContext((state) => state.month);
476	+  const { timezone } = useBookerTime();
477	+
478	+  const monthStart = dayjs.tz(`${month ?? dayjs().format("YYYY-MM")}-01`, timezone);
479	+  // Padded so leading/trailing days shown from adjacent months and multi-day views are covered
480	+  const from = monthStart.subtract(7, "day").toISOString();
481	+  const to = monthStart.add(1, "month").add(14, "day").toISOString();
482	+
483	+  const { data } = useQuery({
484	+    queryKey: ["waitlist-booked-times", eventId, from, to],
485	+    enabled: !!eventId,
486	+    queryFn: async () => {
487	+      const params = new URLSearchParams({ eventTypeId: String(eventId), from, to });
488	+      const res = await fetch(`/api/waitlist/booked-times?${params.toString()}`);
489	+      if (!res.ok) return [];
490	+      const body: { times: string[] } = await res.json();
491	+      return body.times;
492	+    },
493	+  });
494	+
495	+  return useMemo(() => {
496	+    const byDay: Record<string, string[]> = {};
497	+    for (const time of data ?? []) {
498	+      const day = dayjs(time).tz(timezone).format("YYYY-MM-DD");
499	+      (byDay[day] ??= []).push(time);
500	+    }
501	+    return byDay;
502	+  }, [data, timezone]);
503	+};
```

```text
===== internal-tasker.ts
import logger from "@calcom/lib/logger";

import { Task } from "./repository";
import type { TaskTypes } from "./tasker";
import { type TaskerCreate, type Tasker } from "./tasker";

/**
 * This is the default internal Tasker that uses the Task repository to create tasks.
 * It doesn't have any external dependencies and is suitable for most use cases.
 * To use a different Tasker, you can create a new class that implements the Tasker interface.
 * Then, you can use the TaskerFactory to select the new Tasker.
 */
export class InternalTasker implements Tasker {
  create: TaskerCreate = async (type, payload, options = {}): Promise<string> => {
    const payloadString = typeof payload === "string" ? payload : JSON.stringify(payload);
    return Task.create(type, payloadString, options);
  };

  async cleanup(): Promise<void> {
    const count = await Task.cleanup();
    logger.info(`Cleaned up ${count} tasks`);
  }

  async cancel(id: string): Promise<string> {
    const task = await Task.cancel(id);
    return task.id;
  }

  async cancelWithReference(referenceUid: string, type: TaskTypes): Promise<string | null> {
    const task = await Task.cancelWithReference(referenceUid, type);
    return task?.id ?? null;
  }
}
===== task-processor.ts
import { Task } from "./repository";
import tasksMap, { tasksConfig } from "./tasks";

/**
 * TaskProcessor handles the processing of tasks from the queue.
 * This is separated from task creation to avoid importing all task handlers
 * when only creating tasks, which eliminates compilation overhead.
 */
export class TaskProcessor {
  async processQueue(): Promise<void> {
    const tasks = await Task.getNextBatch();
    console.info(`Processing ${tasks.length} tasks`, tasks);

    const tasksPromises = tasks.map(async (task) => {
      console.info(
        `Processing task ${task.id}, attempt:${task.attempts} maxAttempts:${task.maxAttempts} lastFailedAttempt:${task.lastFailedAttemptAt}`,
        task
      );
      const taskHandlerGetter = tasksMap[task.type as keyof typeof tasksMap];
      if (!taskHandlerGetter) throw new Error(`Task handler not found for type ${task.type}`);
      const taskConfig = tasksConfig[task.type as keyof typeof tasksConfig];
      const taskHandler = await taskHandlerGetter();
      return taskHandler(task.payload, task.id)
        .then(async () => {
          await Task.succeed(task.id);
        })
        .catch(async (error) => {
          console.info(`Retrying task ${task.id}: ${error}`);
          await Task.retry({
            taskId: task.id,
            lastError: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error",
            minRetryIntervalMins:
              taskConfig && "minRetryIntervalMins" in taskConfig ? taskConfig.minRetryIntervalMins : null,
          });
        });
    });
    const settled = await Promise.allSettled(tasksPromises);
    const failed = settled.filter((result) => result.status === "rejected");
    const succeded = settled.filter((result) => result.status === "fulfilled");
    console.info({ failed, succeded });
  }
}
===== repository.ts
import { prisma } from "@calcom/prisma";
import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";
import { Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";

import { type TaskTypes } from "./tasker";

const whereSucceeded: Prisma.TaskWhereInput = {
  succeededAt: { not: null },
};

const whereMaxAttemptsReached: Prisma.TaskWhereInput = {
  attempts: {
    equals: {
      // @ts-expect-error prisma is tripping: '_ref' does not exist in type 'FieldRef<"Task", "Int">'
      _ref: "maxAttempts",
      _container: "Task",
    },
  },
};

/** This is a function to ensure new Date is always fresh */
const makeWhereUpcomingTasks = (): Prisma.TaskWhereInput => ({
  // Get only tasks that have not succeeded yet
  succeededAt: null,
  // Get only tasks that are scheduled to run now or in the past
  scheduledAt: {
    lt: new Date(),
  },
  // Get only tasks where maxAttemps has not been reached
  attempts: {
    lt: {
      // @ts-expect-error prisma is tripping: '_ref' does not exist in type 'FieldRef<"Task", "Int">'
      _ref: "maxAttempts",
      _container: "Task",
    },
  },
});

type Dependencies = {
  prismaClient: PrismaClient;
};

export class TaskRepository {
  constructor(private readonly deps: Dependencies) {}

  async create(
    type: TaskTypes,
    payload: string,
    options: { scheduledAt?: Date; maxAttempts?: number; referenceUid?: string } = {}
  ) {
    const { scheduledAt, maxAttempts, referenceUid } = options;
    console.info("Creating task", { type, payload, scheduledAt, maxAttempts });
    const newTask = await this.deps.prismaClient.task.create({
      data: {
        payload,
        type,
        scheduledAt,
        maxAttempts,
        referenceUid,
      },
    });
    return newTask.id;
  }

  async getNextBatch() {
    console.info("Getting next batch of tasks", makeWhereUpcomingTasks());
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
      where: makeWhereUpcomingTasks(),
      orderBy: {
        scheduledAt: "asc",
      },
      take: 1000,
    });
  }

  async getFailed() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
      where: whereMaxAttemptsReached,
    });
  }

  async getSucceeded() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
      where: whereSucceeded,
    });
  }

  async count() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count();
  }

  async countUpcoming() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
      where: makeWhereUpcomingTasks(),
    });
  }

  async countFailed() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
      where: whereMaxAttemptsReached,
    });
  }

  async countSucceeded() {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
      where: whereSucceeded,
    });
  }

  async retry({
    taskId,
    lastError,
    minRetryIntervalMins,
  }: {
    taskId: string;
    lastError?: string;
    minRetryIntervalMins?: number | null;
  }) {
    const failedAttemptTime = new Date();
    const updatedScheduledAt = minRetryIntervalMins
      ? new Date(failedAttemptTime.getTime() + 1000 * 60 * minRetryIntervalMins)
      : undefined;

    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.update({
      where: {
        id: taskId,
      },
      data: {
        attempts: { increment: 1 },
        lastError,
        lastFailedAttemptAt: failedAttemptTime,
        ...(updatedScheduledAt && {
          scheduledAt: updatedScheduledAt,
        }),
      },
    });
  }

  async succeed(taskId: string) {
    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.update({
      where: {
        id: taskId,
      },
      data: {
        attempts: { increment: 1 },
        succeededAt: new Date(),
      },
    });
  }

import { InternalTasker } from "./internal-tasker";
// import { RedisTasker } from "./redis-tasker";
import { type Tasker, type TaskerTypes } from "./tasker";

/**
 * This is a factory class that creates Taskers.
 * The TaskerFactory is useful when you want to use a different Tasker in different environments.
 * For example, you can use the InternalTasker in development and the AWSSQSTasker in production.
 */
export class TaskerFactory {
  createTasker(type?: TaskerTypes): Tasker {
    // TODO: Add more alternative Taskers in the future:
    // RedisTasker, TriggerDevTasker, TemporalIOTasker, AWSSQSTasker, etc.
    // TODO: Uncomment the following line when RedisTasker is implemented.
    // if (type === "redis") return new RedisTasker();
    // For now, we only have the InternalTasker.
    if (type === "internal") return new InternalTasker();
    // Default to InternalTasker
    return new InternalTasker();
  }
}

/** Shorthand for getting the default Tasker */
export function getTasker() {
  const taskerFactory = new TaskerFactory();
  return taskerFactory.createTasker();
}

===== api/cron.ts
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

import { TaskProcessor } from "../task-processor";

async function handler(request: NextRequest) {
  const authHeader = request.headers.get("authorization");
  if (authHeader !== `Bearer ${process.env.CRON_SECRET}`) {
    return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
  }
  const processor = new TaskProcessor();
  await processor.processQueue();
  return NextResponse.json({ success: true });
}

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return await handler(request);
}

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  return await handler(request);
}
```

```text
  public async sendEmail() {
    const featuresRepository = new FeaturesRepository(prisma);
    const emailsDisabled = await featuresRepository.checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally("emails");
    /** If email kill switch exists and is active, we prevent emails being sent. */
    if (emailsDisabled) {
      console.warn("Skipped Sending Email due to active Kill Switch");
      return new Promise((r) => r("Skipped Sending Email due to active Kill Switch"));
    }

    if (process.env.INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE === "true") {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment
      //@ts-expect-error
      setTestEmail(await this.getNodeMailerPayload());
      console.log(
        "Skipped Sending Email as process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_UNIT_TESTS is set. Emails are available in globalThis.testEmails"
      );
      return new Promise((r) => r("Skipped sendEmail for Unit Tests"));
    }

    const payload = await this.getNodeMailerPayload();

    const from = "from" in payload ? (payload.from as string) : "";
    const to = "to" in payload ? (payload.to as string) : "";

    if (isSmsCalEmail(to)) {
      console.log(`Skipped Sending Email to faux email: ${to}`);
      return new Promise((r) => r(`Skipped Sending Email to faux email: ${to}`));
    }

    const sanitizedFrom = sanitizeDisplayName(from);
    const sanitizedTo = sanitizeDisplayName(to);

    const parseSubject = z.string().safeParse(payload?.subject);
    const payloadWithUnEscapedSubject = {
      headers: this.getMailerOptions().headers,
      ...payload,
      ...{
        from: sanitizedFrom,
        to: sanitizedTo,
      },
      ...(parseSubject.success && { subject: decodeHTML(parseSubject.data) }),
    };
    const { createTransport } = await import("nodemailer");
    await new Promise((resolve, reject) =>
      createTransport(this.getMailerOptions().transport).sendMail(
        payloadWithUnEscapedSubject,
        (_err, info) => {
          if (_err) {
            const err = getServerErrorFromUnknown(_err);
            this.printNodeMailerError(err);
            reject(err);
          } else {

        e
      )
    );
```

```text
import { serialize } from "cookie";
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from "next";
import { v4 as uuid } from "uuid";

import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { PrismaSelectedSlotRepository } from "@calcom/features/selectedSlots/repositories/PrismaSelectedSlotRepository";
import { WEBAPP_URL } from "@calcom/lib/constants";
import { MINUTES_TO_BOOK } from "@calcom/lib/constants";
import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";
import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";

import type { TReserveSlotInputSchema } from "./reserveSlot.schema";

interface ReserveSlotOptions {
  ctx: {
    prisma: PrismaClient;
    req?: NextApiRequest | undefined;
    res?: NextApiResponse | undefined;
  };
  input: TReserveSlotInputSchema;
}
export const reserveSlotHandler = async ({ ctx, input }: ReserveSlotOptions) => {
  const { prisma, req, res } = ctx;
  const uid = req?.cookies?.uid || uuid();

  const { slotUtcStartDate, slotUtcEndDate, eventTypeId, _isDryRun } = input;
  const releaseAt = dayjs.utc().add(parseInt(MINUTES_TO_BOOK), "minutes").format();
  const eventType = await prisma.eventType.findUnique({
    where: { id: eventTypeId },
    select: { users: { select: { id: true } }, seatsPerTimeSlot: true },
  });

  if (!eventType) {
    throw new TRPCError({
      message: "Event type not found",
      code: "NOT_FOUND",
    });
  }

  let shouldReserveSlot = true;

  // If this is a seated event then don't reserve a slot
  if (eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot) {
    // Check to see if this is the last attendee
    const bookingWithAttendees = await prisma.booking.findFirst({
      where: {
        eventTypeId,
        startTime: slotUtcStartDate,
        endTime: slotUtcEndDate,
        status: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED,
      },
      select: { attendees: true },
    });
    const bookingAttendeesLength = bookingWithAttendees?.attendees?.length;
    if (bookingAttendeesLength) {
      const seatsLeft = eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot - bookingAttendeesLength;
      if (seatsLeft < 1) shouldReserveSlot = false;
    } else {
      // If there is no booking yet then don't reserve the slot
      shouldReserveSlot = false;
    }
  }

  // Check for existing reservations for the same slot
  const slotsRepo = new PrismaSelectedSlotRepository(prisma);
  const reservedBySomeoneElse = await slotsRepo.findReservedByOthers({
    slot: {
      utcStartIso: slotUtcStartDate,
      utcEndIso: slotUtcEndDate,
    },
    eventTypeId,
    uid,
  });

  if (eventType && shouldReserveSlot && !reservedBySomeoneElse && !_isDryRun) {
    try {
      await Promise.all(
        // FIXME: In case of team event, users doesn't have assignees, those are in hosts. users just have the creator of the event which is wrong.
        // Also, we must not block all the users' slots, we must use routedTeamMemberIds if set like we do in getSchedule.
        // We could even improve it by identifying the next person being booked now that we have a queue of assignees.
        eventType.users.map((user) =>
          prisma.selectedSlots.upsert({
            where: { selectedSlotUnique: { userId: user.id, slotUtcStartDate, slotUtcEndDate, uid } },
            update: {
              slotUtcStartDate,
              slotUtcEndDate,
              releaseAt,
              eventTypeId,
            },
            create: {
              userId: user.id,
              eventTypeId,
              slotUtcStartDate,
              slotUtcEndDate,
              uid,
              releaseAt,
              isSeat: eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot !== null,
            },
          })
        )
      );
    } catch {
      throw new TRPCError({
        message: "Event type not found",
        code: "NOT_FOUND",
      });
    }
  }
  // We need this cookie to be accessible from embeds where the booking flow is displayed within an iframe on a different origin.
  // For third‑party iframe contexts (embeds on other sites), browsers require SameSite=None and Secure to make the cookie available.
  // For local development on http://localhost we fall back to SameSite=Lax to avoid requiring https during development.
  const useSecureCookies = WEBAPP_URL.startsWith("https://");
  res?.setHeader(
    "Set-Cookie",
    serialize("uid", uid, {
      path: "/",
      sameSite: useSecureCookies ? "none" : "lax",
      secure: useSecureCookies,
    })
  );
  return {
    uid: uid,
  };
};
```

```text
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/removeSelectedSlot.schema.ts
import type { PrismaClient } from "@calcom/prisma";
import type { Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";

import type { ISelectedSlotRepository } from "./ISelectedSlotRepository";
import type { TimeSlot } from "./ISelectedSlotRepository";

export class PrismaSelectedSlotRepository implements ISelectedSlotRepository {
  constructor(private prismaClient: PrismaClient) {}

  private async findFirst({ where }: { where: Prisma.SelectedSlotsWhereInput }) {
    return await this.prismaClient.selectedSlots.findFirst({
      where,
    });
  }

  async findReservedByOthers({
    slot,
    eventTypeId,
    uid,
  }: {
    slot: TimeSlot;
    eventTypeId: number;
    uid: string;
  }) {
    return await this.findFirst({
      where: {
        slotUtcStartDate: slot.utcStartIso,
        slotUtcEndDate: slot.utcEndIso,
        eventTypeId,
        uid: { not: uid },
        releaseAt: { gt: new Date() },
      },
    });
  }

  async findManyReservedByOthers(slots: TimeSlot[], eventTypeId: number, uid: string) {
    return await this.prismaClient.selectedSlots.findMany({
      where: {
        OR: slots.map((slot) => ({
          slotUtcStartDate: slot.utcStartIso,
          slotUtcEndDate: slot.utcEndIso,
          eventTypeId,
          uid: { not: uid },
          releaseAt: { gt: new Date() },
        })),
      },
      select: {
        slotUtcStartDate: true,
        slotUtcEndDate: true,
      },
    });
  }

  async findManyUnexpiredSlots({
    userIds,
    currentTimeInUtc,
  }: {
    userIds: number[];
    currentTimeInUtc: string;
  }) {
    return this.prismaClient.selectedSlots.findMany({
      where: {
        userId: { in: userIds },
        releaseAt: { gt: currentTimeInUtc },
      },
      select: {
        id: true,
        slotUtcStartDate: true,
        slotUtcEndDate: true,
        userId: true,
        isSeat: true,
        eventTypeId: true,
        uid: true,
      },
    });
  }

  async deleteManyExpiredSlots({
    eventTypeId,
    currentTimeInUtc,
  }: {
    eventTypeId: number;
    currentTimeInUtc: string;
  }) {
    return this.prismaClient.selectedSlots.deleteMany({
      where: {
        eventTypeId: { equals: eventTypeId },
        releaseAt: { lt: currentTimeInUtc },
      },
    });
  }
}
```

```text
import { HttpError } from "./http-error";
import type { RateLimitHelper } from "./rateLimit";
import { rateLimiter } from "./rateLimit";

export async function checkRateLimitAndThrowError({
  rateLimitingType = "core",
  identifier,
  onRateLimiterResponse,
  opts,
}: RateLimitHelper) {
  const response = await rateLimiter()({ rateLimitingType, identifier, opts });
  if (onRateLimiterResponse) onRateLimiterResponse(response);
  const { success, reset } = response;
  if (!success) {
    const convertToSeconds = (ms: number) => Math.floor(ms / 1000);
    const secondsToWait = Math.max(0, convertToSeconds(reset - Date.now()));
    throw new HttpError({
      statusCode: 429,
      message: `Rate limit exceeded. Try again in ${secondsToWait} seconds.`,
    });
  }
  return response;
}
```

```text
import type { Params } from "app/_types";
import { ApiError } from "next/dist/server/api-utils";
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

import { HttpError } from "@calcom/lib/http-error";
import { getServerErrorFromUnknown } from "@calcom/lib/server/getServerErrorFromUnknown";
import { performance } from "@calcom/lib/server/perfObserver";

import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
import { getHTTPStatusCodeFromError } from "@trpc/server/http";

type Handler<T extends NextResponse | Response = NextResponse> = (
  req: NextRequest,
  { params }: { params: Promise<Params> }
) => Promise<T>;

export const defaultResponderForAppDir = <T extends NextResponse | Response = NextResponse>(
  handler: Handler<T>,
  endpointRoute?: string
) => {
  return async (req: NextRequest, { params }: { params: Promise<Params> }) => {
    let ok = false;
    try {
      performance.mark("Start");
      let result: T | undefined;
      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" || !endpointRoute) {
        result = await handler(req, { params });
      } else {
        const { wrapApiHandlerWithSentry } = await import("@sentry/nextjs");
        result = await wrapApiHandlerWithSentry(async () => await handler(req, { params }), endpointRoute)();
      }

      ok = true;
      if (result) {
        return result;
      }

      return NextResponse.json({});
    } catch (error) {
      let serverError: HttpError;

      if (error instanceof TRPCError) {
        const statusCode = getHTTPStatusCodeFromError(error);
        serverError = new HttpError({ statusCode, message: error.message });
      } else if (error instanceof ApiError) {
        serverError = new HttpError({
          message: error.message,
          statusCode: error.statusCode,
          url: req.url,
          method: req.method,
        });
      } else {
        serverError = getServerErrorFromUnknown(error);
      }

      // Don't report 400-499 errors to Sentry/console
      if (!(serverError.statusCode >= 400 && serverError.statusCode < 500)) {
        console.error(serverError);
        const { captureException } = await import("@sentry/nextjs");
        captureException(error);
      }

      return NextResponse.json(
        {
          message: serverError.message,
          url: serverError.url,
          method: serverError.method,
        },
        {
          status: serverError.statusCode,
        }
      );
    } finally {
      performance.mark("End");
      performance.measure(`[${ok ? "OK" : "ERROR"}][${req.method}] '${req.url}'`, "Start", "End");
    }
  };
};
```

```text
export const AvailableTimes = ({
  slots,
  showTimeFormatToggle = true,
  className,
  date,
  bookedTimes = [],
  ...props
}: AvailableTimesProps) => {
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const { timeFormat, timezone } = useBookerTime();

  const oooAllDay = slots.every((slot) => slot.away);
  if (oooAllDay) {
    return <OOOSlot {...slots[0]} />;
  }

  // A partial-day entry leaves a run of away slots in the middle of the day. One panel stands in for each run,
  // at the first away slot, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window.
  const merged = mergeByTime(slots, date ? bookedTimes : []);
  const isAway = (item: Slot | string | undefined) => typeof item === "object" && !!item.away;
  const items: ReactNode[] = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < merged.length; index++) {
    const slot = merged[index];
    if (typeof slot === "string") {
      items.push(
        <JoinWaitlistButton
          key={slot}
          date={date ?? ""}
          slotStart={slot}
          label={t("waitlist_join_time", { time: dayjs.utc(slot).tz(timezone).format(timeFormat) })}
        />
      );
      continue;
    }
    if (!slot.away) {
      items.push(<SlotItem key={slot.time} slot={slot} {...props} />);
      continue;
    }
    if (isAway(merged[index - 1])) continue;
    let runEnd = index;
    while (isAway(merged[runEnd + 1])) runEnd++;
    items.push(
      <OOOSlot key={`ooo-${slot.time}`} {...slot} className={runEnd === merged.length - 1 ? "pb-0" : ""} />
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className={classNames("text-default flex flex-col", className)}>
      <div className="h-full pb-4">
        {!slots.length && (
          <div
            data-testId="no-slots-available"
            className="bg-subtle border-subtle flex h-full flex-col items-center rounded-md border p-6 dark:bg-transparent">
            <CalendarX2Icon className="text-muted mb-2 h-4 w-4" />
            <p className={classNames("text-muted", showTimeFormatToggle ? "-mt-1 text-lg" : "text-sm")}>
              {t("all_booked_today")}
            </p>
            {date && bookedTimes.length > 0 && (
              <JoinWaitlistButton date={date} label={t("waitlist_join_day")} className="mb-0 mt-4" />
            )}
          </div>
        )}
        {items}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

/** Interleaves booked times (as ISO strings) with open slots in time order, skipping times that are still open. */
const mergeByTime = (slots: Slot[], bookedTimes: string[]): (Slot | string)[] => {
  if (!bookedTimes.length) return slots;
  const openTimes = new Set(slots.map((slot) => dayjs(slot.time).valueOf()));
  const booked = bookedTimes.filter((time) => !openTimes.has(dayjs(time).valueOf()));
```

```text
import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";

import type { Slots, Slot } from "../lib/types";

/**
 * Gets slots for a specific date from the schedule cache.
 * @param date Format YYYY-MM-DD
 * @param scheduleCache Instance of useScheduleWithCache
 */

export const useSlotsForDate = (date: string | null, slots?: Slots) => {
  const slotsForDate = useMemo(() => {
    if (!date || typeof slots === "undefined") return [];
    return slots[date] || [];
  }, [date, slots]);

  return slotsForDate;
};

export const useSlotsForAvailableDates = (dates: (string | null)[], slots?: Slots) => {
  const [slotsPerDay, setSlotsPerDay] = useState<{ date: string | null; slots: Slots[string] }[]>([]);

  const toggleConfirmButton = useCallback((selectedSlot: Slot) => {
    setSlotsPerDay((prevSlotsPerDay) =>
      prevSlotsPerDay.map(({ date, slots }) => ({
        date,
        slots: slots.map((slot) => ({
          ...slot,
          showConfirmButton: slot.time === selectedSlot.time ? !selectedSlot?.showConfirmButton : false,
        })),
      }))
    );
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (slots === undefined) {
      setSlotsPerDay([]);
      return;
    }

    const updatedSlots = dates
      .filter((date) => date !== null)
      .map((date) => ({
        slots: slots[`${date}`] || [],
        date,
      }));

    setSlotsPerDay(updatedSlots);
  }, [JSON.stringify(dates), JSON.stringify(slots)]);

  return { slotsPerDay, setSlotsPerDay, toggleConfirmButton } as const;
};
```

I've finished Phase 1 and Phase 2. I haven't run any tests or changed anything in your checkout: I fetched the PR into a separate reference and read files from there, and your branch and `QUIZ-STUDY-NOTES.md` are untouched.

# Phase 1: Requirements

**Sources read:** Issue #13 (body and its one comment), the PR #125 description, both commits, all 30 changed files, and the AI log (searched for test claims and the author's prompts; not read in full). There are no review comments on the PR yet. It still merges cleanly into the current `main`.

**User story (from the issue):** "As someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for the time I need, so that I am told when it frees up."

The issue has no formal acceptance-criteria section, so I built this list from its "solution" and "scope" sections:

| # | What the issue asks for | Status (from reading the code only) |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | Join a waitlist from a fully booked page, for one time slot or a whole date | **Partial.** Per-time buttons work on partly booked days. The fully booked day looks broken (S1 below). |
| AC2 | When a booking is **cancelled or rescheduled**, notify people in order with a time-limited claim link | **Partial.** Cancellation is handled. Rescheduling is not hooked up: the only trigger is in `handleCancelBooking`. |
| AC3 | Host controls: per-event-type on/off switch, size cap, and a view of who is waiting | **Not met.** None of these exist. |
| AC4 | Leave the waitlist from the email | **Met** (code only). |
| AC5 | "An expiring claim flow that has to resolve a race between claimants" | **Not met.** The slot is only held on the booking page (S2). |
| AC6 | Must respect `seatsPerTimeSlot` | **Not met** (S4). |
| AC7 | New database table and migration; translated UI strings | **Met**, with two caveats: there are two migrations for one new table, and emails are always in English (the author says so). |

**Scope change:** The author's first AI prompt describes a narrower feature: a day-level waitlist plus a 6-hour rule. It leaves out the host controls and the reschedule trigger. The PR never says these were moved out of scope or into a follow-up issue.

**Design decisions and tech-debt section (first look):**
- Both design decisions are written up: the 6-hour claim window, and whole-day vs. single-time waitlists.
- The tech-debt section doesn't list the real debt (booking-page-only hold, English-only email, no host controls, no reschedule trigger). The Q&A does admit the first two.
- "Crontabs had to be made" doesn't match the diff. No cron config was added; the PR reuses the existing tasker cron.

# Phase 2: Lifecycle trace

| Step | Where it happens | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Booker sees a booked time | `useWaitlistBookedTimes.ts` calls `GET /api/waitlist/booked-times`, then `mergeByTime` in `AvailableTimes.tsx` | This now runs on **every** event type's booking page; there's no on/off switch. |
| 2. Joins | `JoinWaitlistButton` calls `POST /api/waitlist`, then `WaitlistService.join` | Input checked with zod; rate limit is 10 per minute per IP. |
| 3. Stored | `WaitlistRepository.create` | Duplicates are checked in code only. The database doesn't prevent them. |
| 4. Cancel | `handleCancelBooking.ts:431-448` queues an `offerWaitlistSpot` task | Seat cancellations return earlier (`:310-327`), so they never get here. |
| 5. Find who's next | `offerSpot` then `findOldestWaitingForTime` | First come, first served by `createdAt`. |
| 6. Notify | `offerSpot`: mark entry OFFERED, create a 6h slot hold, schedule the expiry task, send email | Four separate steps, not in one transaction. |
| 7. Claim link | `/api/waitlist/claim` sets the `uid` cookie and redirects to the booker with the slot preselected | Cookie flags match the existing `reserveSlot` handler. |
| 8. Book | The existing booking flow | Nothing on the server checks the waitlist hold. |
| 9. Update entry | `expireOffer`, 6 hours later | Marked CLAIMED only if the booking email matches the waitlist email. |
| 10. Next person | `expireOffer` or `leave` hands the slot to the next person | Works by code reading. |

# Suspected serious issues (none verified by a test yet)

**S1. A fully booked day shows an empty panel (High).**
- In `AvailableTimes.tsx:274-276`, `slots.every(s => s.away)` is `true` when `slots` is empty.
- So it returns `<OOOSlot/>`, and `OutOfOfficeInSlots` returns `null` when there's no out-of-office user.
- The "All booked" box with the new day-level button (around line 320) is never reached.
- The early return is old upstream code. This PR is what now lets users select fully booked days and reach it.
- This would break design decision 2 and the main scenario in the issue.
- The AI log never shows the full flow confirmed in a browser. Its last debugging message is "I still haven't found the cause."

**S2. The 6-hour hold doesn't survive the booking page (High).** The claim route sets the `uid` cookie to the entry's uid. Then:
- `reserveSlot` cuts the hold's expiry to 5 minutes (`reserveSlot.handler.ts:83-101`).
- When the waitlister picks a different time or leaves the page, `useSlots` calls `removeSelectedSlotMark` (`useSlots.ts:150-152`). That deletes **every** hold for that uid (`_router.tsx:46-54`).
- The author mentions the 5-minute cut, but not the deletion.
- Result: the person opens the link, closes the tab, and the slot is open to anyone. Their entry stays OFFERED for 6 hours, so nobody else on the waitlist gets it, and the email's promise ("holding it for you until X") is broken.

**S3. `offerSpot` isn't safe to retry (Medium).** It marks the entry OFFERED first, then creates the hold, schedules the expiry, and sends the email.
- If the hold or expiry step throws, the tasker retries the task (default 3 attempts). The retry gives the same slot to the **next** person.
- The first entry can be left OFFERED with no expiry task, so it's stuck.
- Email failures don't trigger this, because `BaseEmail.sendEmail` catches its own errors.

**S4. Seated events never get offers (Medium).** Cancelling one seat returns before the waitlist code runs. Separately, `offerSpot` treats any other booking at that time as "rebooked." The same check blocks round-robin events whenever another host has a booking at that time.

**Needs Phase 3 checking:** `booked-times` returns booking start times for any `eventTypeId`, with no check that the event type is public. I haven't yet compared it with what `getSchedule` exposes, so I'm not calling it a vulnerability.

**Good work worth noting:**
- `transition()` uses a conditional `updateMany` (compare-and-set), so two processes can't both claim the same entry.
- The leave link shows a confirmation page and only acts on POST, so email link scanners can't remove people.
- Claim and leave links use unguessable UUIDs.
- The service gets its dependencies passed in (clock, email sender), which makes it easy to test.

**Process and standards:**
- The PR is about 1,270 lines of code across 28 code files, against the project's guideline of under 500 lines and 10 files.
- `getWaitlistService` builds its objects by hand instead of going through the dependency-injection container.
- The two migrations for one new table should be combined into one.
- The tests are 12 service-level tests against a fake repository. There are none for the API routes, the UI, the cancel hook, or the repository queries.

# Next step: verify before going further

S2 depends on browser behavior, so it belongs in your manual Test C/D.

```text
import { generatorHandler } from "@prisma/generator-helper";
import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";

const header = `// This file was generated by a custom prisma generator, do not edit manually.\n`;

generatorHandler({
  onManifest() {
    return {
      defaultOutput: "./enums/index.ts",
      prettyName: "Prisma Enum Generator",
    };
  },
  async onGenerate(options) {
    const enums = options.dmmf.datamodel.enums;

    const output = enums.map((e) => {
      let enumString = `export const ${e.name} = {\n`;
      e.values.forEach(({ name: value }) => {
        enumString += `  ${value}: "${value}",\n`;
      });
      enumString += `} as const;\n\n`;
      enumString += `export type ${e.name} = (typeof ${e.name})[keyof typeof ${e.name}];\n`;

      return enumString;
    });

    const outputFile = options.generator.output;
    if (!outputFile || !outputFile.value) {
      throw new Error("No output file specified");
    }

    const outputPath = path.resolve(outputFile.value);
    await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(outputPath), { recursive: true });
```

```text
// 09:00 to 16:00 UTC on 2026-10-08, one slot an hour. The hours listed are away.

  Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, index) => {
    const hour = 9 + index;
    const time = `2026-10-08T${String(hour).padStart(2, "0")}:00:00.000Z`;
    return awayHours.includes(hour) ? { time, away: true, ...awayData } : { time };
  });

const renderDay = (slots: Slot[]) => render(<AvailableTimes slots={slots} event={{ data: null }} />);

// The hours of the slot buttons that come before and after the panel in document order.
const hoursAround = (panel: HTMLElement) => {
  const hourOf = (button: HTMLElement) => Number(button.dataset.time?.slice(11, 13));
  const buttons = screen.getAllByTestId("time");
  return {
    before: buttons
      .filter((button) => button.compareDocumentPosition(panel) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING)
      .map(hourOf),
    after: buttons
      .filter((button) => button.compareDocumentPosition(panel) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING)
      .map(hourOf),
  };
};
```

```text
import { vi, describe, it, expect, afterEach } from "vitest";

// We want to test that the UID cookie set by reserveSlotHandler is configured with the correct
// SameSite and Secure attributes depending on the environment (http vs https).
// reserveSlotHandler relies on WEBAPP_URL being evaluated at import time, so we need to reset modules
// between tests after tweaking process.env to simulate different deployment environments.
//
// The handler also calls into Prisma and the SelectedSlotRepository, so we stub those parts out.

// We alias the module path once we know WEBAPP_URL has been configured.
const dynamicImportHandler = async () => await import("./reserveSlot.handler");

// The repository instance method is used to check for an existing reservation by someone else.
// To keep this unit test isolated from the database layer, we stub this to always resolve falsey.
vi.mock("@calcom/features/selectedSlots/repositories/PrismaSelectedSlotRepository", () => ({
  PrismaSelectedSlotRepository: vi.fn().mockImplementation(function () {
    return {
      findReservedByOthers: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(null),
    };
  }),
}));

// A tiny helper to build a canned handler context with stubbed Prisma methods.
const buildContext = () => {
  const prismaStub = {
    eventType: {
      // Return a minimal event type that will exercise the happy path.
      findUnique: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ users: [{ id: 1 }], seatsPerTimeSlot: null }),
    },
    booking: {
      findFirst: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(null),
    },
    selectedSlots: {
      upsert: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(null),
    },
  } as unknown as any;

  // Capture header values to assert on.
  let cookieHeaderValue: string | null = null;
  const resStub = {
    setHeader: vi.fn((_name: string, value: string) => {
      cookieHeaderValue = value;
    }),
  };

  const reqStub = {
    cookies: {},
  };

  return { prismaStub, resStub, reqStub, getCookieHeader: () => cookieHeaderValue };
};

describe("reserveSlotHandler cookie settings", () => {
  const originalWebappUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL;

  afterEach(() => {
    // Reset the module registry and restore the WEBAPP_URL between tests.
    vi.resetModules();
    if (originalWebappUrl === undefined) {
      delete process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL;
    } else {
      process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL = originalWebappUrl;
    }
  });

  it("sets SameSite=None and Secure when WEBAPP_URL is https", async () => {
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL = "https://example.com";
    vi.resetModules();
    const { reserveSlotHandler } = await dynamicImportHandler();
    const { prismaStub, reqStub, resStub, getCookieHeader } = buildContext();
    await reserveSlotHandler({
      ctx: { prisma: prismaStub, req: reqStub, res: resStub },
      input: {
        slotUtcStartDate: new Date().toISOString(),
        slotUtcEndDate: new Date(Date.now() + 15 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
        eventTypeId: 1,
        bookingUid: undefined,
        _isDryRun: false,
      },
    });
```

```typescript
// REVIEW-ONLY regression test for PR #125 (S3). Lives only in a scratch clone; never committed.
import { WaitlistStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import type { WaitlistEntryDto, WaitlistRepository } from "../repositories/WaitlistRepository";
import { WaitlistService } from "./WaitlistService";

const HOUR = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const NOW = Date.parse("2026-11-01T12:00:00Z");
type Row = WaitlistEntryDto & { dayStart: Date; dayEnd: Date; slotStart: Date | null; seq: number };

// Mirrors the real repository's semantics: transition() is a conditional updateMany (compare-and-set).
function makeRepo() {
  const rows: Row[] = [];
  const holds: string[] = [];
  let seq = 0;
  let failNextHold = false;
  const repo = {
    findWaitingByEmailAndDay: async () => null,
    create: async (d: Omit<Row, "id" | "uid" | "status" | "seq" | "hostUserId" | "offerStart" | "offerEnd" | "offerExpiresAt">) => {
      seq++;
      const row: Row = { ...d, id: seq, uid: `uid-${seq}`, status: WaitlistStatus.WAITING, hostUserId: null, offerStart: null, offerEnd: null, offerExpiresAt: null, seq };
      rows.push(row);
      return row;
    },
    findById: async (id: number) => rows.find((r) => r.id === id) ?? null,
    findByUid: async (uid: string) => rows.find((r) => r.uid === uid) ?? null,
    findOldestWaitingForTime: async (q: { time: Date }) =>
      rows
        .filter((r) => r.status === WaitlistStatus.WAITING && r.dayStart <= q.time && r.dayEnd > q.time)
        .sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq)[0] ?? null,
    transition: async (id: number, from: WaitlistStatus, to: WaitlistStatus, offer?: object | null) => {
      const row = rows.find((r) => r.id === id);
      if (!row || row.status !== from) return false;
      row.status = to;
      if (offer) Object.assign(row, offer);
      return true;
    },
    findEventTypeForWaitlist: async () => ({ id: 1, title: "Intro", slug: "intro", length: 30, team: null, owner: { username: "host" }, users: [] }),
    createSlotHold: async (h: { uid: string }) => {
      if (failNextHold) {
        failNextHold = false;
        throw new Error("simulated transient DB error inserting SelectedSlots");
      }
      holds.push(h.uid);
    },
    deleteSlotHolds: async () => {},
    findActiveBookingAttendeeEmailsAt: async () => null,
    findActiveBookingStartTimes: async () => [],
  };
  return { repo: repo as unknown as WaitlistRepository, rows, holds, failHoldOnce: () => { failNextHold = true; } };
}

describe("S3: offerSpot is not idempotent", () => {
  let fake: ReturnType<typeof makeRepo>;
  let service: WaitlistService;
  const scheduleOfferExpiry = vi.fn();
  const sendOfferEmail = vi.fn();
  const slot = { eventTypeId: 1, hostUserId: 9, start: new Date(NOW + 46 * HOUR), end: new Date(NOW + 46.5 * HOUR) };

  beforeEach(async () => {
    fake = makeRepo();
    scheduleOfferExpiry.mockReset();
    sendOfferEmail.mockReset();
    service = new WaitlistService({ waitlistRepo: fake.repo, webappUrl: "https://app.test", scheduleOfferExpiry, sendOfferEmail, now: () => NOW });
    await service.join({ eventTypeId: 1, name: "a", email: "first@x.com", timeZone: "UTC", date: "2026-11-03" });
    await service.join({ eventTypeId: 1, name: "b", email: "second@x.com", timeZone: "UTC", date: "2026-11-03" });
  });

  it("S3a: a tasker retry after a partial failure must not offer the same slot to a second person", async () => {
    fake.failHoldOnce();
    await expect(service.offerSpot(slot)).rejects.toThrow(); // attempt 1 fails -> tasker schedules a retry
    await service.offerSpot(slot); // attempt 2 (retry of the same task payload)

    const offered = fake.rows.filter((r) => r.status === WaitlistStatus.OFFERED).map((r) => r.email);
    console.log("S3a OFFERED entries:", offered, "holds:", fake.holds, "expiry scheduled for:", scheduleOfferExpiry.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]), "emails:", sendOfferEmail.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0].email));
    expect(offered).toEqual(["first@x.com"]);
  });

  it("S3b: the first entry must not be left OFFERED with no expiry task (stuck forever)", async () => {
    fake.failHoldOnce();
    await expect(service.offerSpot(slot)).rejects.toThrow();
    await service.offerSpot(slot);
    const first = fake.rows[0];
    const expiryIds = scheduleOfferExpiry.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0]);
    console.log("S3b first entry status:", first.status, "expiry scheduled for ids:", expiryIds);
    expect(first.status === WaitlistStatus.OFFERED && !expiryIds.includes(first.id)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("S3c: the same task processed twice concurrently must still produce one offer", async () => {
    await Promise.all([service.offerSpot(slot), service.offerSpot(slot)]);
    const offered = fake.rows.filter((r) => r.status === WaitlistStatus.OFFERED).map((r) => r.email);
    console.log("S3c OFFERED entries:", offered, "emails:", sendOfferEmail.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0].email));
    expect(offered).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```typescript
      },
      upsert: async ({ where, update, create }: { where: { selectedSlotUnique: Hold }; update: Partial<Hold>; create: Hold }) => {
        const k = where.selectedSlotUnique;
        const row = holds.find(
          (h) => h.uid === k.uid && h.userId === k.userId && t(h.slotUtcStartDate) === t(k.slotUtcStartDate) && t(h.slotUtcEndDate) === t(k.slotUtcEndDate)
        );
        if (row) Object.assign(row, { releaseAt: new Date(update.releaseAt as Date) });
        else holds.push({ ...create, releaseAt: new Date(create.releaseAt) });
      },
      deleteMany: async ({ where }: { where: { uid: string | { equals: string } } }) => {
        const uid = typeof where.uid === "string" ? where.uid : where.uid.equals;
        for (let i = holds.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (holds[i].uid === uid) holds.splice(i, 1);
      },
    },
  };
  return { prisma, holds };
}

const ENTRY_UID = "waitlist-entry-uid";
const start = new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 3600_000);
const end = new Date(start.getTime() + 30 * 60_000);
const SIX_HOURS = 6 * 3600_000;

async function offerHold(prisma: ReturnType<typeof fakePrisma>["prisma"]) {
  // Exactly what WaitlistService.offerSpot does via the real repository
  // biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny: review-only fake
  await new WaitlistRepository(prisma as any).createSlotHold({
    uid: ENTRY_UID, eventTypeId: 1, userId: 9, start, end, releaseAt: new Date(Date.now() + SIX_HOURS),
  });
}

describe("S2: the 6-hour waitlist hold once the waitlister opens the claim link", () => {
  it("S2a: booker's reserveSlot (cookie uid = entry uid, as set by /api/waitlist/claim) must not shorten the 6h hold", async () => {
    const { prisma, holds } = fakePrisma();
    await offerHold(prisma);
    const { reserveSlotHandler } = await import("./reserveSlot.handler");
    await reserveSlotHandler({
      // biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny: review-only fake
      ctx: { prisma: prisma as any, req: { cookies: { uid: ENTRY_UID } } as any, res: { setHeader: vi.fn() } as any },
      input: { slotUtcStartDate: start.toISOString(), slotUtcEndDate: end.toISOString(), eventTypeId: 1, _isDryRun: false },
    });
    const minutesLeft = (t(holds[0].releaseAt) - Date.now()) / 60_000;
    console.log("S2a hold rows:", holds.length, "minutes left on hold after reserveSlot:", minutesLeft.toFixed(1));
    expect(minutesLeft).toBeGreaterThan(5 * 60);
  });

  it("S2b: booker's removeSelectedSlotMark (fires when the waitlister changes time / leaves) must not delete the 6h hold", async () => {
    const { prisma, holds } = fakePrisma();
    await offerHold(prisma);
    const { slotsRouter } = await import("./_router");
    // biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noExplicitAny: review-only fake
    const caller = slotsRouter.createCaller({ prisma, req: { cookies: { uid: ENTRY_UID } } } as any);
    await caller.removeSelectedSlotMark({ uid: ENTRY_UID });
    console.log("S2b hold rows after removeSelectedSlotMark:", holds.length);
    expect(holds).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```text
export function rateLimiter() {

      error: err.message,
      stack: err.stack,
      identifier,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    });
    return { success: true, limit: 10, remaining: 999, reset: 0 };
```

```typescript
// REVIEW-ONLY test for PR #125 (Phase 5). Lives only in a scratch clone; never committed.
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import type { WaitlistRepository } from "../repositories/WaitlistRepository";
import { WaitlistService } from "./WaitlistService";

function serviceCapturing(now: string) {
  const created: { dayStart: Date; dayEnd: Date }[] = [];
  const repo = {
    findEventTypeForWaitlist: async () => ({ id: 1 }),
    findWaitingByEmailAndDay: async () => null,
    create: async (d: { dayStart: Date; dayEnd: Date }) => {
      created.push(d);
      return d;
    },
  } as unknown as WaitlistRepository;
  const service = new WaitlistService({
    waitlistRepo: repo,
    webappUrl: "https://app.test",
    scheduleOfferExpiry: async () => {},
    sendOfferEmail: async () => {},
    now: () => Date.parse(now),
  });
  const join = (date: string, timeZone: string) =>
    service.join({ eventTypeId: 1, name: "a", email: "a@x.com", timeZone, date });
  return { join, created };
}

const iso = (d: { dayStart: Date; dayEnd: Date }) => [d.dayStart.toISOString(), d.dayEnd.toISOString()];

describe("Phase 5: whole-day waitlist boundaries", () => {
  it("ordinary day in New York is midnight-to-midnight local", async () => {
    const s = serviceCapturing("2026-10-01T00:00:00Z");
    await s.join("2026-11-03", "America/New_York");
    expect(iso(s.created[0])).toEqual(["2026-11-03T05:00:00.000Z", "2026-11-04T05:00:00.000Z"]);
  });

  it("DST fall-back day (25h) in New York ends at the next local midnight", async () => {
    const s = serviceCapturing("2026-10-01T00:00:00Z");
    await s.join("2026-11-01", "America/New_York");
    expect(iso(s.created[0])).toEqual(["2026-11-01T04:00:00.000Z", "2026-11-02T05:00:00.000Z"]);
  });

  it("DST spring-forward day (23h) in New York ends at the next local midnight", async () => {
    const s = serviceCapturing("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z");
    await s.join("2026-03-08", "America/New_York");
    expect(iso(s.created[0])).toEqual(["2026-03-08T05:00:00.000Z", "2026-03-09T04:00:00.000Z"]);
  });

  it("an impossible calendar date (2026-02-30) is rejected, not silently moved", async () => {
    const s = serviceCapturing("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z");
    const result = await s.join("2026-02-30", "UTC").then(
      () => `accepted, stored ${JSON.stringify(s.created.map(iso))}`,
      (e: Error) => `rejected: ${e.message}`
    );
    expect(result).toMatch(/^rejected/);
  });
});
```

```text
# Issue #13 -- Booking waitlist

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](13-zachbowden-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](13-zachbowden-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1-2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

The two most important classes are `WaitlistService` and `AvailableTimes`.
* `WaitlistService` (new) holds all of the waitlist rules: it rejects joins less than 6 hours out, offers a freed slot to the person who has been waiting longest, holds the slot for 6 hours, and passes the slot to the next person when an offer expires or someone leaves.
* `AvailableTimes` (modified) is where the booker sees the waitlist. It merges this event's booked times into the open time slots as "Time - Join waitlist" buttons, and only shows the whole-day button when there are no open slots left.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

The most significant relationship is `handleCancelBooking` queueing the `offerWaitlistSpot` task, which calls `WaitlistService.offerSpot()`. This is what connects the existing cancellation flow to the waitlist: a cancellation frees a slot, and the task offers it to the waitlist in the background so cancelling a booking is never slowed down or broken by the waitlist. `offerSpot()` also schedules `expireWaitlistOffer` for 6 hours later, which is how unclaimed spots move on to the next person.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

The slot hold is only enforced on the booking page (other bookers don't see the held slot), not by the booking endpoint itself, and it is shortened to the normal 5 minute reservation once the waitlister clicks the slot. I would enforce the hold on the server so it fully lasts the 6 hours. I would also store the booker's locale when they join so the offer email isn't always in English.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

The sequence starts when the booker opens the booking page and sees a booked time as "6:00am - Join waitlist". The successful outcome is that after the host's booking is cancelled, the booker is emailed that the spot opened up, the slot is held for them for 6 hours, and they claim and book it.

2. Identify the 2-3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

* The booking page calls `GET /booked-times` and merges the booked times with the open slots (`mergeByTime`), which is what makes a taken time show up as a waitlist option (new code, in a modified existing component).
* When the host cancels, `handleCancelBooking` marks the booking cancelled (existing code) and queues `offerWaitlistSpot` on the tasker (new code). The tasker cron then runs `offerSpot`, which marks the entry as offered, holds the slot in `SelectedSlots` and sends the email (new code using the existing slot reservation table).
* Six hours later `expireOffer` checks whether the slot was booked: if the waitlister booked it the entry is claimed, if someone else did they keep their place, and if it is still free it is offered to the next person (new code).

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

* Validation failures when joining (bad email, day or time less than 6 hours away) return an error toast. Left out because it is standard input validation.
* Opening an expired or already used claim link returns a "this offer has expired" response instead of redirecting. Left out to keep the claim path readable.
* Leaving the waitlist before any offer was made just marks the entry as left without offering anything. Left out because nothing else happens in that case.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```
